docs.title: What is Linkboy?
docs.text: Linkboy (aka Linking Boy on iOS) is a GBA emulator, making it possible to run classic games on modern mobile devices. Among many other things, it emulates Game Link Cable, allowing you to play multi-player games through local networks.

docs.title: Contact Us
docs.text:
We would like to hear back from you!

For any questions, bug report, or feature request regarding Linkboy, please contact us at support@pixelrespawn.com.

docs.title: Creating skins
docs.text:
You can download skins from the skin gallery and extract their .lbskin packages for further study. If your archive tool does not recognize the extension, rename a copy to .zip before extracting it.

Follow these steps to create a controller skin for Linkboy. The skin specification describes the file formats and available options in detail.

docs.title: 1. Choose a skin type
docs.text:
Decide what you want to customize:

  • Control skin: changes the appearance of controls while using an existing layout profile.
  • Full skin: includes layouts that position the game screen, controls, and any background or overlay artwork.

Create a folder to hold your skin’s files.

docs.title: 2. Create info.json
docs.text:
Create a file named info.json in your skin folder with a unique ID and a display name. You can also include your name in the optional author field:

{
  "id": "com.example.my_skin",
  "name": "My skin",
  "author": "Your name"
}

Choose an ID following the skin identifier rules, and keep it unchanged when updating the same skin. For a full skin, you will add layout entries in step 4.

docs.title: 3. Prepare your images
docs.text:
Create your artwork as PNG images. Use transparency where appropriate, and keep PNG file sizes as small as possible—larger files take longer to load.

Name button and D-pad images according to the control image naming rules. For example, use A.png for the A button and optionally A_pressed.png for its pressed state.

For a full skin, you can also create backgrounds and overlays. Choose their filenames yourself; you will reference them in the layout files. See Background and overlay images for how these images are positioned and layered.

docs.title: 4. Create your layouts
docs.text:
Skip this step for a control skin.

Choose a virtual canvas size for each layout you want to provide, such as 1080 × 2400 for a portrait layout. Create a JSON file that defines both game screen rectangles (gbaScreen and gbcScreen), your controls, and any background or overlay images.

Use the example layout as a starting point, and see Layout files for the available fields.

If the controls are drawn into your background or overlay image, set each control’s frame to match the position and size of its drawing. Set its alpha to 0 so only the artwork is visible, while the control remains touchable.

Add your layout files to info.json, including each file’s virtual canvas dimensions:

{
  "id": "com.example.my_skin",
  "name": "My skin",
  "author": "Your name",
  "layouts": [
    {
      "width": 1080,
      "height": 2400,
      "file": "portrait.json"
    },
    {
      "width": 2400,
      "height": 1080,
      "file": "landscape.json"
    }
  ]
}

Include only the layouts you have created. See Layout entries for how Linkboy selects and scales layouts for different screens.

docs.title: 5. Package your skin
docs.text:
Check that all referenced layouts and images are present in your skin folder. File paths are relative to this folder, which will become the archive root.

ZIP the contents of the folder so info.json is at the archive root, then rename the archive from .zip to .lbskin. See Package format for details.

docs.title: 6. Try it in Linkboy
docs.text:
Install your skin in Linkboy. For a full skin, create a layout profile from it. For a control skin, apply it to a profile that was not created from a full skin.

Try the skin in a game and adjust your artwork or layouts as needed. When testing updated full-skin layouts, create a new profile if you have edited the previous one.

docs.title: 7. Share your skin
docs.text:
Share the finished .lbskin file with users. Include a screenshot and a description of the layouts you designed it for.

Want to have your skin hosted on our website? Contact us.

docs.title: Game thumbnails
docs.text: Linkboy can display thumbnails next to game names, making your library easier to browse and recognize. Linkboy does not provide or distribute thumbnail images — you are always in control of where thumbnails come from.

docs.title: Setting a thumbnail manually
docs.text:
You can set a custom thumbnail for any game directly from the app:

  1. From the Game Library Long-press a game and tap Choose thumbnail from the top-right menu. Then choose an image from your device to use as the game's thumbnail.

  2. From the Recents screen Long-press a recently played game, then select Set as thumbnail from the popup menu. The thumbnail will be generated from the game’s most recent saved state.

Manually set thumbnails override any downloaded thumbnails for that game.

docs.title: Downloading thumbnails from your own server
docs.text:
Linkboy can also download thumbnails from a server URL that you provide for each system.

  • The URL must end with a slash /, indicating it points to a directory.
  • Filenames must follow the No-Intro naming convention.
  • Thumbnail images must use the .png extension.

For example, if your server URL is http://thumbnails.example.com/gba/ and a game's No-Intro name is My Game, Linkboy will try to download the game's thumbnail image from: http://thumbnails.example.com/gba/My%20Game.png

Note

After setting URLs, you may need to rescan your games for thumbnails to appear. This only needs to be done once.

docs.title: Import saves
docs.text:
Note

Only in-game saves (as opposed to state saves) can be shared between emulators.

The following steps demonstrate how to import saves from the My Boy! emulator:

  1. In Linkboy, tap the Settings tab on the bottom. Scroll down, find and tap Open app folder. A file manager will show up.

  2. In the file manager, click the 3-bar icon on the top-left, scroll down and tap My Boy!.

    Note

    If you can't find it, please update My Boy! to the latest version.

  3. The file manager should now show the internal file structure of My Boy!. Tap the save subfolder.

  4. Select all the files ending with .sav that you would like to import by tapping the icons on the left side of the file names.

    Tip

    • If the file names are too long and hard to read, it may be helpful to switch to list view and landscape mode.

    • You can select all files regardless of their types, but only .sav files will be recognized by Linkboy.

  5. Tap the 3-dot icon on the top-right, choose Copy to…

  6. Once again, click the 3-bar icon on the top-left but choose Linkboy this time.

  7. The file manager should now show the internal file structure of Linkboy. Tap the saves subfolder.

    Note

    The saves folder may not have been created if you have not yet used Linkboy to play a game. In that case, you can manually create one with the file manager.

  8. Tap the Copy button, which will copy all your selected files to this folder.

    Note

    If there are already files with the same names, they will be renamed to .bak before being overwritten.

  9. Now switch back to Linkboy. Start your game, tap the menu button, and then the 3-bar icon. Tap 'Reboot game'. The game will restart and your new .sav file will be picked up by the emulator.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
Effective date: [09/03/2025]

Linkboy (“the App”), also known as Linking Boy on iOS, is a Game Boy Advance emulator. We respect your privacy and are committed to being transparent about how we handle your information.

docs.title: Information We Collect
docs.text: The App itself does not collect or store any personal information on our servers. However, certain features involve third-party services:

docs.title: 1. RetroAchievements
docs.text:
• If you choose to log in to your RetroAchievements account, your username and password are transmitted securely to RetroAchievements’ servers for authentication, and Linkboy stores your RetroAchievements username and a secure login token on your device to maintain your session until you sign out in Linkboy settings. Your password is never stored on your device.
  • Any data transmitted to RetroAchievements is sent to their servers, which are located in Nuremberg, Germany.
  • Gameplay information, such as game identification, achievement progress, and leaderboard scores, may be sent to RetroAchievements so these features work.
  • Linkboy does not transmit personal data to its own servers. Any data sent to RetroAchievements is managed by RetroAchievements, who provide mechanisms for data access, correction, and deletion in accordance with GDPR.

docs.title: 2. Google Drive Sync
docs.text:
• If you choose to sync with Google Drive, the App requests access using the drive.file permission.
  • Only save files and cheats created by Linkboy are uploaded, and the App does not have access to any other files in your Google Drive.
  • You can revoke access at any time in your Google Account settings.

docs.title: Data Sharing
docs.text: Data is only transmitted to the services you explicitly connect (RetroAchievements and Google Drive) so their features can function.

docs.title: Your Choices
docs.text:
• You can use the App without signing in to RetroAchievements or enabling Google Drive sync.
  • You may revoke Google Drive permissions at any time via your Google Account.
  • You may manage or delete your RetroAchievements account directly through the RetroAchievements website.

docs.title: Children’s Privacy
docs.text:
Linkboy is not specifically directed to children under 13.

  • The App may be used by people of all ages, but we recommend parental guidance for younger users.
  • We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13.
  • Features that involve signing into RetroAchievements or syncing with Google Drive require an account, which should be managed by a parent or guardian if used by a child under 13.

docs.title: Contact Us
docs.text: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at: support@pixelrespawn.com

docs.title: ROM patching
docs.text:
Linkboy supports automatic ROM patching when a game is loaded. Here's how to set it up:

Important

Your game must have been added by "Game folders". Otherwise, Linkboy won't have permission to locate and read your patch file.

  1. Enable "Auto patch ROM" in the settings.

  2. Place the matching patch file (.ips, .ups or .bps) in the same folder as your game file.

    Note

    The patch file must have the same name as the game file (excluding the extension). Example: your_rom.gba and your_rom.ips

  3. Launch your game — it should be automatically patched. If it isn't and you've followed all instructions, the most likely reason is that the patch doesn't match your game or its version.

docs.title: Skin specification
docs.text: This reference describes the file structure and JSON format used to create controller skins for Linkboy.

docs.title: Package format
docs.text:
A Linkboy skin package is a ZIP archive with a filename ending in .lbskin. The archive must contain info.json at its root.

Any file referenced in info.json or a layout JSON file can use a path relative to the archive root. For example, you can place layout files in layouts/ and background or overlay images in images/, then reference them as layouts/portrait.json and images/background.png. Paths are always relative to the archive root, even when the referring layout file is in a subdirectory.

Control images are looked up by the naming convention described under Control images, rather than by a file field.

Example file Purpose info.json Skin identifier, display name, and layout entries layout-1080x2400.json A layout for a reference canvas of 1080 × 2400 background-1080x2400.png Artwork referenced by a layout A.png Base image for the A button A_pressed.png Optional pressed image for the A button dpad.png Base image for the D-pad dpad_u.png Optional image for the up direction

Use valid JSON with quoted property names and no comments or trailing commas. Match the capitalization shown for input names and control filenames.

docs.title: Skin metadata: info.json
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id String Yes Unique skin identifier, for example com.example.skins.my_skin name String Yes Display name shown to users author String No Creator's name layouts Array of layout entries No Defaults to []

docs.title: Skin identifier
docs.text:
The skin ID must start with a letter or digit and may contain only ASCII letters (A–Z, a–z), digits (0–9), dots (.), underscores (_), and hyphens (-).

We recommend a fully qualified reverse-domain-style identifier, such as com.example.skins.my_skin, to help avoid conflicts with other skins. Keep the identifier stable when updating the same skin.

docs.title: Layout entries
docs.text:
Each layout entry contains:

Field Type Required Description width Integer Yes Virtual canvas width height Integer Yes Virtual canvas height file String Yes Layout JSON path relative to the archive root 
{
  "id": "com.example.my_skin",
  "name": "My skin",
  "author": "Pixel Respawn",
  "layouts": [
    { "width": 1080, "height": 2400, "file": "layout-1080x2400.json" },
    { "width": 2400, "height": 1080, "file": "layout-2400x1080.json" }
  ]
}

The width and height define a virtual canvas. All coordinates and sizes in that layout JSON file relate to this canvas. Linkboy converts them to real screen coordinates at runtime; the canvas dimensions do not have to match the device’s screen resolution.

Linkboy chooses the best layout according to the screen’s aspect ratio and resolution. When two layouts have very close aspect ratios, it chooses the layout whose canvas size is closest to the screen resolution.

If the chosen layout’s virtual canvas size differs from the screen size, Linkboy scales the layout to fit the screen while preserving its aspect ratio, then centers it on the screen.

A control skin can omit layouts:

{
  "id": "com.example.skins.my_controls",
  "name": "My controls",
  "author": "Example Studio"
}

docs.title: Layout files
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Purpose gbaScreen Rectangle Yes — GBA game screen placement gbcScreen Rectangle Yes — GB/GBC game screen placement controls Array of controls No [] Touch controls backgrounds Array of images No [] Background artwork overlays Array of images No [] Overlay artwork

docs.title: Rectangles
docs.text:
All rectangles use the following four required integer fields. Coordinates are measured from the top-left of the layout’s virtual canvas: x increases to the right and y increases downward.

Field Meaning x Left position y Top position width Rectangle width height Rectangle height 
{ "x": 0, "y": 286, "width": 1080, "height": 720 }

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Purpose input Input object Yes — D-pad or button mapping frame Rectangle Yes — Control position and size alpha Number from 0 to 1 No 1 Control image opacity

alpha is inclusive of both endpoints: 0 is invisible, 1 is fully opaque, and values between them are partially transparent. An invisible control remains touchable. Set alpha to 0 when the control artwork is already drawn into a background or overlay.

docs.title: Button input
Supported keys
docs.text:
Key names are case-sensitive. The table below lists them in declaration order, which also determines the filename order for combined inputs. Read each row from left to right, then continue to the next row.

Category Names Directional Up, Down, Left, Right Console A, B, L, R, Select, Start Turbo TurboA, TurboB, TurboL, TurboR Save states Load, Save Speed FastForward, SlowMotion Other actions Screenshot, Menu

docs.title: D-pad input
docs.text:
For a standard D-pad, use:

{ "type": "dpad" }

The up, down, left, and right fields define the input for each D-pad direction. Each accepts a single key name from Supported keys, such as "Up" or "A". Arrays are not supported. All four fields are optional; omit them to use the standard directional inputs.

Field Default up "Up" down "Down" left "Left" right "Right"

docs.title: Background and overlay images
docs.text:
Images and controls are displayed in this order, from back to front:

  1. Background images (backgrounds).
  2. The game screen.
  3. Overlay images (overlays).
  4. All controls.

Both backgrounds and overlays contain image objects:

Field Type Required Default Purpose frame Rectangle Yes — Image position and size file String Yes — Image path relative to the archive root alpha Number from 0 to 1 No 1 Image opacity 
{
  "frame": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1080, "height": 2400 },
  "file": "images/background.png",
  "alpha": 1
}

docs.title: Example layout
docs.text:
This abbreviated example illustrates the structure.

{
  "gbaScreen": { "x": 0, "y": 286, "width": 1080, "height": 720 },
  "gbcScreen": { "x": 0, "y": 160, "width": 1080, "height": 972 },
  "backgrounds": [
    {
      "frame": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1080, "height": 2400 },
      "file": "background-1080x2400.png"
    }
  ],
  "controls": [
    {
      "input": { "type": "dpad" },
      "frame": { "x": 40, "y": 1580, "width": 440, "height": 440 }
    },
    {
      "input": { "type": "button", "key": "A" },
      "frame": { "x": 878, "y": 1688, "width": 164, "height": 164 }
    },
    {
      "input": { "type": "button", "key": "B" },
      "frame": { "x": 658, "y": 1748, "width": 164, "height": 164 }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Control images
docs.text: Linkboy looks up control images by filename; individual controls do not have an image filename field.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
Use the key name for the base image and append _pressed for the optional pressed image.

For combined inputs, Linkboy joins the key names with + in the declaration order shown in Supported keys, regardless of their order in the JSON array. For example, a button combining A, B, Select, and Start uses A+B+Select+Start.png and optionally A+B+Select+Start_pressed.png.

Control Base image Optional pressed image A A.png A_pressed.png B B.png B_pressed.png L / R L.png / R.png L_pressed.png / R_pressed.png Select / Start Select.png / Start.png Select_pressed.png / Start_pressed.png Turbo A TurboA.png TurboA_pressed.png Turbo B TurboB.png TurboB_pressed.png Turbo L TurboL.png TurboL_pressed.png Turbo R TurboR.png TurboR_pressed.png Load state Load.png Load_pressed.png Save state Save.png Save_pressed.png Fast-forward FastForward.png FastForward_pressed.png Slow motion SlowMotion.png SlowMotion_pressed.png Screenshot Screenshot.png Screenshot_pressed.png Menu Menu.png Menu_pressed.png A+B A+B.png A+B_pressed.png

If a button’s pressed image is omitted, its base image is used in both states.

docs.title: D-pad
docs.text:
State Filename Neutral / base dpad.png Up dpad_u.png Down dpad_d.png Left dpad_l.png Right dpad_r.png Up-left dpad_ul.png Up-right dpad_ur.png Down-left dpad_dl.png Down-right dpad_dr.png

All directional images are optional. Any missing directional image uses dpad.png. Supply only dpad.png for a static D-pad.

docs.title: Default skin fallback
docs.text:
If a control’s base image is absent, Linkboy uses the default skin’s image for that control. This lets a skin replace selected controls without supplying a complete image set.

If the base image is present but a pressed or directional image is absent, the supplied base image is used for that state.

docs.title: Invalid controls
docs.text: Controls that fail deserialization, such as a button with an unknown key name or a control missing a required rectangle field, are skipped individually. If a control does not appear, check its JSON and key spelling. This does not mean a malformed JSON document or an invalid top-level layout can be loaded.

docs.title: Using skins
docs.text: Controller skins change the appearance of Linkboy’s on-screen controller. This feature is available in Linkboy version 4.0.0 or later.

docs.title: Download a skin
docs.text: Choose a skin from the skin gallery and save its .lbskin file to your device. Do not extract it.

docs.title: Install a skin
docs.text:
1. Open Linkboy’s Settings and go to Virtual controller → Layouts & skins.
  2. Tap +, then Install skin.
  3. Select the downloaded .lbskin file and confirm installation.

Depending on its type, the installed skin appears under Full skins or Control skins.

docs.title: Full skins
docs.text:
Full skins include layouts and artwork, such as backgrounds, overlays, and control images. To use a full skin, create a layout profile from it:

  1. Under Full skins, find the installed skin.
  2. Tap the + icon next to the skin to create a profile.

The new profile appears under Layout profiles and is automatically selected.

You can use the profile as it is or edit its layout anytime—for example, to move or resize controls, adjust the game screen, or add buttons.

When a full skin is updated, its updated layouts are not applied to existing profiles you have edited—for example, by adding buttons. To use the updated layout, create a new profile from the updated skin.

docs.title: Control skins
docs.text:
Control skins change the control images used by your active layout profile while keeping its layout.

If a layout profile was created from a full skin, it always uses that skin. Selecting a control skin does not override it.

Select a skin under Control skins to apply it to your active profile. To return to the standard control images, select Default skin.
